claim: Distributed neural activity patterns are widely proposed to underlie object identification and categorization in the brain.
source: Distributed neural activity patterns are widely proposed to underlie object identification and categorization in the brain.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established scientific consensus.

claim: Pattern-based representations of odor objects are encoded in piriform cortex.
source: In the olfactory domain, pattern-based representations of odor objects are encoded in piriform cortex.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge about olfactory processing.

claim: Baclofen is a GABA(B) agonist known to attenuate piriform associative inputs.
source: Administration of baclofen, a GABA(B) agonist known to attenuate piriform associative inputs, interfered with within-category pattern separation in piriform cortex
evidence: This is established knowledge about the pharmacological properties of baclofen.

claim: Baclofen interfered with within-category pattern separation in piriform cortex.
source: Administration of baclofen, a GABA(B) agonist known to attenuate piriform associative inputs, interfered with within-category pattern separation in piriform cortex
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from the fMRI pattern analysis.

claim: The magnitude of baclofen-induced change in piriform cortex predicted perceptual alterations in fine-odor discrimination performance.
source: the magnitude of this drug-induced change predicted perceptual alterations in fine-odor discrimination performance.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis between neural and behavioral measures.

claim: Baclofen reduced pattern separation between odor categories in orbitofrontal cortex.
source: Comparatively, baclofen reduced pattern separation between odor categories in orbitofrontal cortex
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental fMRI data.

claim: Baclofen impeded within-category generalization in hippocampus.
source: and impeded within-category generalization in hippocampus.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental fMRI data.

claim: Odor categorization is a dynamic process concurrently engaging stimulus discrimination and generalization at different stages of olfactory information processing.
source: Our findings suggest that odor categorization is a dynamic process concurrently engaging stimulus discrimination and generalization at different stages of olfactory information processing
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings from multiple brain regions.

claim: Associative networks are important in maintaining categorical boundaries.
source: and highlight the importance of associative networks in maintaining categorical boundaries.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effects of baclofen on categorical representations.

claim: Sensory systems must generalize across different objects sharing similar features while maintaining the specificity of individual objects and categories.
source: Importantly, sensory systems must generalize across different objects sharing similar features, but at the same time maintain the specificity of individual objects and categories (Roach, 1978; Riesenhuber and Poggio, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Mechanisms of pattern recognition have been proposed to underlie the neural basis of object categorization.
source: Mechanisms of pattern recognition have been proposed to underlie the neural basis of object categorization, which requires a balance between generalizing inputs across a certain range of variations (known as pattern completion) and discriminating between distinct inputs (known as pattern separation) (Riesenhuber and Poggio, 2000; Haberly, 2001; Wilson and Sullivan, 2011; Chapuis and Wilson, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Pattern completion refers to generalizing inputs across a certain range of variations.
source: which requires a balance between generalizing inputs across a certain range of variations (known as pattern completion)
evidence: This is a definition based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Pattern separation refers to discriminating between distinct inputs.
source: and discriminating between distinct inputs (known as pattern separation) (Riesenhuber and Poggio, 2000; Haberly, 2001; Wilson and Sullivan, 2011; Chapuis and Wilson, 2012).
evidence: This is a definition based on established scientific knowledge and citations.

claim: Pattern recognition computations can be achieved by associating sensory inputs with internal templates established through experience and encoded into memory.
source: Such computations can be achieved by associating sensory inputs with internal templates that are established through a lifetime of experience and encoded into memory (Bar, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Associative areas in the visual ventral stream support processes of object categorization.
source: Most neuroscientific research on pattern recognition has concentrated on the visual system, where associative areas in the visual ventral stream and the CA3 region of the hippocampus have been shown to support processes of object categorization (Riesenhuber and Poggio, 2000; Yassa and Stark, 2011; Haxby et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The CA3 region of the hippocampus supports processes of object categorization.
source: Most neuroscientific research on pattern recognition has concentrated on the visual system, where associative areas in the visual ventral stream and the CA3 region of the hippocampus have been shown to support processes of object categorization (Riesenhuber and Poggio, 2000; Yassa and Stark, 2011; Haxby et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Different odor objects evoke distinguishable ensemble activity patterns without spatial topography in piriform cortex.
source: In the olfactory system, information in a whiff of scented air is transformed into distributed patterns of neural activity in the piriform cortex, with both animal and human studies demonstrating that different odor objects evoke distinguishable ensemble activity patterns without spatial topography (Wilson and Sullivan, 2011; Gottfried, 2010; Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Howard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: fMRI multivariate patterns in posterior piriform cortex encode odor identity and category information.
source: Recent work has revealed that fMRI multivariate patterns in posterior piriform cortex (PPC) encode not only odor identity, but also category information (e.g., minty or woody), whereby odor patterns belonging to the same category are more similar (more overlapping) than those across different categories (Howard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Odor patterns belonging to the same category are more similar than those across different categories in posterior piriform cortex.
source: Recent work has revealed that fMRI multivariate patterns in posterior piriform cortex (PPC) encode not only odor identity, but also category information (e.g., minty or woody), whereby odor patterns belonging to the same category are more similar (more overlapping) than those across different categories (Howard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Piriform cortex is the largest subregion of primary olfactory cortex.
source: As the largest subregion of primary olfactory cortex, the piriform cortex receives afferent (bottom-up) inputs from the olfactory bulb through the lateral olfactory tract
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Piriform cortex receives afferent inputs from the olfactory bulb through the lateral olfactory tract.
source: As the largest subregion of primary olfactory cortex, the piriform cortex receives afferent (bottom-up) inputs from the olfactory bulb through the lateral olfactory tract
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Piriform cortex receives extensive associative inputs from orbitofrontal cortex, amygdala, and entorhinal cortex.
source: and extensive associative (top-down) inputs from higher-order association areas such as orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), amygdala, and entorhinal cortex (Carmichael et al., 1994; Johnson et al., 2000; Haberly and Price, 1978; Insausti et al., 1987; Insausti et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior anatomical research.

claim: The convergence of bottom-up and top-down projections in piriform cortex, along with dense recurrent collaterals, is thought to support olfactory pattern recognition and associative learning.
source: This convergence of bottom-up and top-down projections, along with the presence of dense recurrent collaterals, is thought to support olfactory pattern recognition and associative learning (Haberly, 2001; Haberly and Bower, 1989; Wilson, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Rats can learn to discriminate or ignore detectable differences between highly overlapping odor mixtures.
source: For example, when confronted with highly overlapping odor mixtures, rats can learn to discriminate or ignore detectable differences between these mixtures, with piriform activity patterns exhibiting either separation (enhanced discrimination) or completion (enhanced generalization), respectively (Chapuis and Wilson, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Piriform activity patterns exhibit either separation or completion depending on whether rats discriminate or ignore differences between odor mixtures.
source: For example, when confronted with highly overlapping odor mixtures, rats can learn to discriminate or ignore detectable differences between these mixtures, with piriform activity patterns exhibiting either separation (enhanced discrimination) or completion (enhanced generalization), respectively (Chapuis and Wilson, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Posterior piriform cortex is a substrate for odor discrimination in humans.
source: Evidence from humans has also pointed to PPC as a substrate for odor discrimination (Li et al., 2008) and categorization (Howard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Posterior piriform cortex is a substrate for odor categorization in humans.
source: Evidence from humans has also pointed to PPC as a substrate for odor discrimination (Li et al., 2008) and categorization (Howard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Piriform cortex is capable of modulating pattern representations along a discrimination-generalization spectrum to encode behaviorally adaptive meaning through perceptual experience.
source: Together these findings suggest that piriform cortex is capable of modulating pattern representations along a discrimination-generalization spectrum in order to encode behaviorally adaptive meaning through perceptual experience.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited research findings.

claim: Theoretical modelling and empirical evidence propose that piriform associative connections are essential for odor recognition.
source: While theoretical modelling and empirical evidence propose that piriform associative connections are essential for odor recognition (Haberly, 2001)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: One week of sensory deprivation resulted in a reduction of odor-evoked mean activity in posterior piriform cortex without alteration of pattern-based piriform representations of odor categories.
source: In a previous fMRI study, human subjects were deprived of afferent sensory input for one week, resulting in a reduction of odor-evoked mean activity in PPC, without alteration of pattern-based piriform representations of odor categories (Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Baclofen selectively suppresses synaptic transmission of association fibers into piriform cortex but leaves afferent inputs from the olfactory bulb unaffected.
source: Baclofen selectively suppresses synaptic transmission of association fibers into piriform cortex, but leaves afferent inputs from the olfactory bulb unaffected (Tang and Hasselmo, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In vivo local application of baclofen in the piriform cortex of anesthetized rats modified the strength of odor-evoked responses of pyramidal neurons by blocking broadly-tuned neurons and increasing odor-selective responses.
source: In vivo local application of baclofen in the piriform cortex of anesthetized rats modified the strength of odor-evoked responses of pyramidal neurons, by blocking broadly-tuned neurons and increasing odor-selective responses (Poo and Isaacson, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Injection of baclofen into the piriform cortex following an olfactory fear conditioning session resulted in fear memory generalization in behaving animals.
source: In behaving animals, injection of baclofen into the piriform cortex following an olfactory fear conditioning session resulted in fear memory generalization, indicating that piriform associative connections are essential for consolidation of stimulus-specific memories (Barnes and Wilson, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Piriform associative connections are essential for consolidation of stimulus-specific memories.
source: In behaving animals, injection of baclofen into the piriform cortex following an olfactory fear conditioning session resulted in fear memory generalization, indicating that piriform associative connections are essential for consolidation of stimulus-specific memories (Barnes and Wilson, 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation from cited research.

claim: The experiment spanned 5 days.
source: The experiment spanned 5 days (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design shown in the figure.

claim: On day 1, subjects underwent pre-drug cognitive and psychophysical testing and fMRI scanning.
source: On day 1, subjects underwent pre-drug cognitive and psychophysical testing and fMRI scanning (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Subjects were administered either placebo (n = 18) or increasing doses of baclofen (n = 14) for 5 consecutive days in a double-blind design.
source: They were subsequently administered either placebo (n = 18) or increasing doses of baclofen (n = 14) for 5 consecutive days, in a double-blind design.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The 5-day schedule was adopted to reach a target dose of 50-mg baclofen while minimizing the occurrence of side effects.
source: This 5-day schedule was adopted to reach a target dose of 50-mg baclofen while minimizing the occurrence of side effects (Terrier et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a methodological decision supported by a citation.

claim: After taking the final dose on day 5, subjects underwent the same testing and fMRI scanning procedures as in the pre-drug session.
source: After taking the final dose on day 5, subjects underwent the same testing and fMRI scanning procedures as in the pre-drug session.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: During scanning, subjects completed an olfactory categorization task and a control visual categorization task.
source: During scanning, subjects completed an olfactory categorization task, as well as a control visual categorization task to establish the sensory specificity of the imaging findings.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Baclofen did not generally compromise cognitive or perceptual performance.
source: We first established that baclofen did not generally compromise cognitive or perceptual performance.
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data presented in Table 1.

claim: There were no significant differences between baclofen and placebo groups on neuropsychological assessments of basic cognition, short-term memory, visual attention, or task switching.
source: Specifically, we found no significant differences between baclofen and placebo groups on neuropsychological assessments of basic cognition, short-term memory, visual attention, or task switching (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: The most common adverse reaction to baclofen medication is transient drowsiness.
source: We also collected subjective reports of sleepiness using the Stanford Sleepiness Scale (SSS) during test sessions, given that the most common adverse reaction to baclofen medication is transient drowsiness (RxList The internet Drug Index, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a drug reference.

claim: Baclofen subjects reported feeling sleepier after taking the drug.
source: Baclofen subjects reported feeling sleepier after taking the drug (Figure 2)
evidence: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Reaction times during the fMRI categorization task did not differ between baclofen and placebo subjects.
source: though reaction times during the fMRI categorization task did not differ from placebo subjects (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Placebo and baclofen groups did not differ on olfactory measures of detection threshold, identification, fine odor discrimination, or intensity and pleasantness ratings.
source: Finally, we examined whether baclofen altered general odor perception. Placebo and baclofen groups did not differ on olfactory measures of detection threshold, identification, fine odor discrimination (Figure 3d), or intensity and pleasantness ratings (for stimuli used in the main fMRI experiment) (Table 1)
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1 and Figure 3d.

claim: Within-category descriptor ratings were significantly higher than across-category descriptor ratings during the pre-drug session.
source: During the pre-drug session, within-category descriptor ratings were significantly higher than across-category descriptor ratings (simple main effect of category at pre: F1,31 = 572.66, P < 0.001; mixed-model ANOVA) (Figure 3a,b)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 3.

claim: There was no interaction between placebo and baclofen groups in within-category versus across-category descriptor ratings during the pre-drug session.
source: in the absence of an interaction between placebo and baclofen groups (F1,30 = 0.0019, P = 0.97; Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data.

claim: During the pre-drug session, within-category odor pairs were rated as significantly more similar than across-category odor pairs.
source: Moreover, during the pre-drug session, the within-category odor pairs were rated as significantly more similar than across-category odor pairs (simple main effect of category at pre: F1,31 = 125.80, P < 0.001; Figure 3c)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Both placebo and baclofen subjects successfully grouped the six odors into three classes appropriately in both pre- and post-drug sessions based on cluster analysis.
source: Finally, based on group averages of similarity ratings, we performed a cluster analysis and found that both placebo and baclofen subjects successfully group the six odors into three classes appropriately in both pre- and post-drug sessions (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is supported by cluster analysis shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Subjects were highly familiar with the odor categories prior to initiating the experiment.
source: These data confirm that subjects were highly familiar with the odor categories prior to initiating the experiment.
evidence: This is an inference from the behavioral data on categorization performance.

claim: There was a main effect of session on categorization showing a general improvement based on similarity ratings.
source: There was a main effect of session on categorization showing a general improvement based on similarity ratings (F1,30 = 5.65, P = 0.024), probably reflecting a practice effect.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: The session-related changes in categorization did not differ between placebo and baclofen groups.
source: However, the session-related changes did not differ between groups (F1,30 = 0.30, P = 0.59; Figure 3c, Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Baclofen did not affect behavioral measures of odor categorization at the group level.
source: Collectively, these results indicated that baclofen did not affect behavioral measures of odor categorization at the group level.
evidence: This is an inference from the behavioral data analysis.

claim: In the pre-drug session, subjects categorized odors with high accuracy (84.4% ± 2.7%, chance level at 33%).
source: In the pre-drug session, subjects categorized odors with high accuracy (84.4% ± 2.7%, chance level at 33%, t31 = 19.37, P < 0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Neither catch trial accuracies nor reaction times differed significantly as a function of treatment group from pre- to post-drug session.
source: Of note, neither the catch trial accuracies nor reaction times (RT) differed significantly as a function of treatment group from pre- to post-drug session (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Significant above-chance decoding accuracy was found in posterior piriform cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, amygdala, and posterior hippocampus across all subjects in the pre-drug session.
source: Across all subjects in the pre-drug session, we found significant above-chance decoding accuracy in PPC (t31 = 2.05, P = 0.024), OFC (t31 = 1.96, P = 0.029), amygdala (t31 = 3.17, P = 0.0017), and posterior hippocampus (pHIP, t31 = 1.90, P = 0.034; Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by SVM classification analysis shown in Figure 4c.

claim: There was a significant session × category type × drug interaction effect in posterior piriform cortex.
source: This yielded a significant session × category type × drug interaction effect (F1,30 = 5.49, P = 0.026) in the absence of other main effects or two-way interactions (all P's >0.15), and suggests that baclofen significantly affected the categorical structure of odor pattern representations in PPC.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Baclofen significantly affected the categorical structure of odor pattern representations in posterior piriform cortex.
source: This yielded a significant session × category type × drug interaction effect (F1,30 = 5.49, P = 0.026) in the absence of other main effects or two-way interactions (all P's >0.15), and suggests that baclofen significantly affected the categorical structure of odor pattern representations in PPC.
evidence: This is an inference from the statistical analysis of fMRI data.

claim: In placebo subjects, the interaction of session × category type was significant in posterior piriform cortex.
source: In placebo subjects the interaction of session × category type was significant in PPC (F1,17 = 9.35, P = 0.0071; repeated-measures ANOVA)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: No session × category type interaction was identified in the baclofen group in posterior piriform cortex.
source: whereas no such interaction was identified in the baclofen group (F1,13 = 0.62, P = 0.45).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: There was a significant increase of within-category odor distance in the placebo group in posterior piriform cortex.
source: This effect was driven by a significant increase of the within-category odor distance in the placebo group (F1,17 = 5.23, P = 0.035)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: There was no significant change in within-category odor distance in the baclofen group in posterior piriform cortex.
source: but not in the baclofen group (F1,13 = 2.61, P = 0.13)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: There was a significant difference in within-category odor distance changes between placebo and baclofen groups in posterior piriform cortex.
source: with a significant difference between groups (F1,30 = 7.36, P = 0.011; mixed-model ANOVA, session × group interaction).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Across-category odor distances did not differ for either placebo or baclofen groups in posterior piriform cortex.
source: On the other hand, across-category odor distances did not differ for either group (placebo, F1,17 = 0.75, P = 0.40; baclofen, F1,13 = 0.27, P = 0.61) or between groups (F1,30 = 0.00014, P = 0.99, Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Repeated exposure to odors in absence of drug induced pattern separation or differentiation in posterior piriform cortex.
source: These results highlight a divergence in PPC pattern representations for odors belonging to the same category, but only in the placebo group. One implication is that repeated exposure to the odors (in absence of drug) induced pattern separation or differentiation, a process that appears to be blocked in the presence of baclofen.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Baclofen blocks the process of pattern separation or differentiation in posterior piriform cortex.
source: These results highlight a divergence in PPC pattern representations for odors belonging to the same category, but only in the placebo group. One implication is that repeated exposure to the odors (in absence of drug) induced pattern separation or differentiation, a process that appears to be blocked in the presence of baclofen.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Prolonged passive exposure to one target odor increased its discriminability from categorically related odors in an earlier olfactory perceptual learning study.
source: Interestingly, this conceptualization – greater pattern separation over time in the control subjects – is in close accordance with an earlier olfactory perceptual learning study from our lab, where prolonged passive exposure to one target odor increased its discriminability from categorically related odors (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Baclofen interferes with the natural emergence of olfactory pattern separation in posterior piriform cortex.
source: Viewed in this context, it is reasonable to speculate that baclofen interferes with the natural emergence of olfactory pattern separation in PPC, possibly reflecting a disruption in consolidation mechanisms that normally underlie perceptual learning.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and prior research.

claim: There was a significant correlation between perceptual performance change and the degree of odor-evoked pattern separation in posterior piriform cortex.
source: We found a significant correlation between perceptual performance change and the degree of odor-evoked pattern separation in PPC (ρ = 0.51, P = 0.031, one-tailed; Figure 5d).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Subjects with less within-category odor separation in posterior piriform cortex showed greater difficulty in discriminating between odors sharing semantic features.
source: Thus, subjects with less within-category odor separation in PPC showed greater difficulty in discriminating between odors sharing semantic features.
evidence: This is an inference from the correlation analysis.

claim: There was no significant correlation between pre-post changes in sleep scale ratings and changes in fine odor discrimination performance across baclofen subjects.
source: To investigate this possibility, we tested the correlation between pre-post changes in sleep scale ratings and changes in fine odor discrimination performance across baclofen subjects. This relationship was not significant (Spearman ρ = -0.33, P = 0.25, n = 14).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis.

claim: There was no significant correlation between sleep scale changes and within-category pattern distance changes in posterior piriform cortex across baclofen subjects.
source: Likewise, there was no significant correlation between sleep scale changes and within-category pattern distance changes in PPC across baclofen subjects (Spearman ρ = 0.11, P = 0.70, n = 14).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis.

claim: There was no direct evidence of a systematic link between sleepiness and odor discrimination at the behavioral or neural level.
source: These data suggest that there was no direct evidence of a systematic link between sleepiness and odor discrimination at the behavioral or neural level.
evidence: This is an inference from the correlation analyses.

claim: Significant three-way interactions of session × category type × drug were found in orbitofrontal cortex and posterior hippocampus.
source: Significant three-way interactions of session × category type × drug were found in OFC (F1,30 = 4.48, P = 0.043) and pHIP (F1,30 = 5.90, P = 0.021) without other main effects or two-way interactions.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: No significant interaction was observed in amygdala.
source: No significant interaction was observed in amygdala (F1,30 = 0.047, P = 0.83; Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: In orbitofrontal cortex, the session × category interaction approached significance in the baclofen group.
source: We found that in OFC, the session × category interaction approached significance in the baclofen group (F1,13 = 4.14, P = 0.063)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: In orbitofrontal cortex, there was a significant decrease in across-category distances in the baclofen group.
source: driven by a significant decrease in across-category distances (F1,13 = 5.93, P = 0.030; Figure 6a)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The decrease in across-category distances in orbitofrontal cortex led to a net effect of category disruption in the baclofen group.
source: and leading to a net effect of category disruption (that is, greater convergence of across-category patterns; e.g., C1 and M1 becoming more alike, Figure 5a).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: There was no categorical change in orbitofrontal cortex in the placebo group.
source: There was no categorical change in the placebo group (session × category interaction, F1,17 = 0.17, P = 0.69).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: In posterior hippocampus, there was a significant session × category interaction in the placebo group.
source: By contrast, in pHIP, there was a significant session × category interaction in the placebo group (F1,17 = 7.68, P = 0.013)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: In posterior hippocampus, there was a trend decrease in within-category distances in the placebo group.
source: here driven by a trend decrease in within-category distances (F1,17 = 3.09, P = 0.097, Figure 6b)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The trend decrease in within-category distances in posterior hippocampus gave rise to an enhanced categorical structure among odors in the placebo group.
source: and giving rise to an enhanced categorical structure among odors (that is, greater convergence of within-category patterns; e.g., C1 and C2 becoming more alike, Figure 5a).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: The profile of changes in posterior hippocampus is opposite to that seen in posterior piriform cortex.
source: Of note, this profile is opposite to that seen in PPC (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is a comparison of the fMRI pattern data across regions.

claim: There was no categorical change in posterior hippocampus in the baclofen group.
source: On the contrary, there was no categorical change in the baclofen group (session × category interaction, F1,13 = 0.77, P = 0.40).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: Baclofen had selective effects on odor category coding in posterior piriform cortex, orbitofrontal cortex, and posterior hippocampus.
source: The above findings indicate that baclofen had selective effects on odor category coding in PPC, OFC, and pHIP.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the fMRI pattern analyses.

claim: There was no effect of baclofen on response accuracies and reaction times in the visual categorization task.
source: There was no effect of baclofen on response accuracies and reaction times (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Category decoding accuracy was significantly above chance in lateral occipital complex across all subjects in the pre-drug session.
source: Across all subjects in the pre-drug session, category decoding accuracy was significantly above chance in LOC (t30 = 2.33, P = 0.013)
evidence: This is supported by SVM classification analysis.

claim: Category decoding accuracy was not significantly above chance in fusiform cortex or in any of the olfactory ROIs for the visual task.
source: but not in fusiform cortex (t30 = -1.20, P = 0.88) or in any of the olfactory ROIs (PPC: t30 = 0.36, P = 0.72; OFC: t30 = -1.36, P = 0.18; amygdala: t30 = -2.47, P = 0.99; pHIP: t30 = 0.078, P = 0.47; Figure 7b).
evidence: This is supported by SVM classification analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: A three-way session × category type × drug interaction was not significant in lateral occipital complex.
source: A three-way session × category type × drug interaction was not significant in LOC (F1,29 = 0.46, P = 0.50; Figure 7c)
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the fMRI pattern data shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Baclofen did not alter coding of categories in the visual domain.
source: suggesting that baclofen did not alter coding of categories in the visual domain.
evidence: This is an inference from the statistical analysis of visual fMRI data.

claim: The impact of baclofen on category coding in posterior piriform cortex was specific to olfaction.
source: Finally, we compared the effect of baclofen on categorization between olfactory and visual tasks, and found that the impact of baclofen on category coding in PPC was specific to olfaction.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of olfactory and visual fMRI data.

claim: A mixed four-way ANOVA revealed a significant interaction of modality × category × session × drug.
source: A mixed four-way ANOVA (three within-subject factors of modality, category type, and session; one between-subject factor of group) revealed a significant interaction of modality × category × session × drug (F1,29 = 4.41, P = 0.044).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis comparing olfactory and visual data.

claim: Baclofen did not alter visual categorization compared to placebo.
source: Thus, while baclofen blocked within-category separation in PPC, it did not alter the visual categorization compared to placebo (category × session × drug interaction: F1,29 = 0.056, P = 0.81).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the visual fMRI data.

claim: The observed effect of baclofen in posterior piriform cortex was not due to generic changes in semantic processing, non-specific changes in hemodynamic parameters, but instead was due to alterations in information coding in the presence of olfactory inputs.
source: These findings imply that the observed effect of baclofen in PPC was not due to generic changes in semantic processing, nor to non-specific changes in hemodynamic parameters, but instead was due to alterations in information coding in the presence of olfactory inputs.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of olfactory and visual data.

claim: In posterior piriform cortex, baclofen interfered with the emergent pattern separation of odors belonging to the same categorical class.
source: We found that in PPC, baclofen (compared to placebo) interfered with the emergent pattern separation of odors belonging to the same categorical class.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding from the fMRI pattern analysis.

claim: Baclofen disrupted across-category separation in olfactory downstream region of orbitofrontal cortex.
source: In contrast, baclofen disrupted across-category separation in olfactory downstream region of OFC
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding from the fMRI pattern analysis.

claim: Baclofen impeded within-category generalization in posterior hippocampus.
source: and impeded within-category generalization in pHIP.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding from the fMRI pattern analysis.

claim: The baclofen effect observed in posterior piriform cortex was opposite to the original prediction that baclofen would simply weaken the boundaries between categories.
source: Interestingly, the baclofen effect observed in PPC was opposite to our original prediction that baclofen would simply weaken the boundaries between categories, leading to reduced pattern separation between citrus, mint, and wood odors.
evidence: This is a comparison of the findings to the original hypothesis.

claim: There was increased pattern separation for within-category odors over time, but specifically in the placebo group.
source: Instead, there was increased pattern separation for within-category odors over time, but specifically in the placebo group, likely reflecting perceptual training or stimulus-specific consolidation from the pre- to post-session.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data.

claim: The significant group × session interaction implies that the natural process of within-category pattern separation in controls was disrupted in the presence of baclofen.
source: The significant group × session interaction implies that the natural process of within-category pattern separation in controls was disrupted in the presence of baclofen.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the statistical interaction.

claim: Piriform associative input normally supports the separation of patterns corresponding to unique identities of individual odors, especially those sharing perceptual features and associated with the same semantic labels.
source: We speculate that piriform associative input normally supports the separation of patterns corresponding to unique identities of individual odors, especially those sharing perceptual features and associated with the same semantic labels.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Perceptual learning enhances discriminability of within-category odor pairs, with concomitant fMRI changes in posterior piriform cortex and orbitofrontal cortex.
source: This mechanism would be compatible with prior work showing that perceptual learning enhances discriminability of within-category odor pairs, with concomitant fMRI changes in PPC as well as OFC (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Piriform cortex has the capacity to enhance either pattern separation or completion, as a function of task demands.
source: One plausible explanation is that piriform cortex has the capacity to enhance either pattern separation or completion, as a function of task demands (Chapuis and Wilson, 2012; Li et al., 2008; Shakhawat et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Various rodent paradigms of olfactory associative learning have shown that the direction of piriform pattern changes can flexibly match the behavioral requirements for either odor discrimination or odor generalization.
source: Various rodent paradigms of olfactory associative learning have shown that the direction of piriform pattern changes can flexibly match the behavioral requirements for either odor discrimination (i.e., pattern separation) or odor generalization (i.e., pattern completion).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from prior research.

claim: The experimental design might have helped stabilize category-specific differences in posterior piriform cortex, even in the presence of baclofen, though at the expense of within-category odor separation.
source: As such, our experimental design might have helped stabilize category-specific differences in PPC, even in the presence of baclofen, though at the expense of within-category odor separation.
evidence: This is speculation about the experimental design's influence on the results.

claim: The fact that categorical representations of citrus, mint, and wood odors were already highly familiar to the subjects could have created further stability against across-category pattern changes.
source: The fact that categorical representations of citrus, mint, and wood odors were already highly familiar to the subjects also could have created further stability against across-category pattern changes.
evidence: This is speculation about factors influencing the results.

claim: The majority (~75%) of trials in the experiment belonged to non-repetition trials.
source: That the majority (~75%) of trials in our experiment belonged to non-repetition trials suggests that category repetitions would not have had a pronounced effect on the findings.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the trial structure.

claim: The proportion of category repetition versus non-repetition trials (per imaging run) was not associated with the strength of pattern categorization effects in posterior piriform cortex.
source: In additional analyses (see Materials and methods), the proportion of category repetition versus non-repetition trials (per imaging run) was not associated with the strength of pattern categorization effects in PPC
evidence: This is supported by additional statistical analyses.

claim: Posterior piriform cortex patterns evoked by the same odor under repetition and non-repetition conditions were not significantly different.
source: and PPC patterns evoked by the same odor under repetition and non-repetition conditions were not significantly different.
evidence: This is supported by additional statistical analyses.

claim: The sequence order of the odors did not have an impact on categorical pattern coding in posterior piriform cortex, either at baseline or in the context of drug.
source: Thus, it is reasonable to conclude that the sequence order of the odors did not have an impact on categorical pattern coding in PPC, either at baseline or in the context of drug.
evidence: This is an inference from the additional analyses.

claim: In orbitofrontal cortex, the discrete categorical patterns for citrus, mint, and wood became less separated in the presence of baclofen.
source: Thus in OFC, the discrete categorical patterns for citrus, mint, and wood became less separated, in the presence of baclofen.
evidence: This is a summary of the fMRI pattern findings in OFC.

claim: Baclofen had no perceptual effect on categorical discrimination.
source: In spite of these changes, there was no parallel impact on behavior. Indeed, baclofen had no perceptual effect on categorical discrimination
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data.

claim: The existence of an odor category necessitates an association between an olfactory stimulus and semantic conceptual knowledge.
source: However, to the extent that the existence of an odor category necessitates an association between an olfactory stimulus and semantic conceptual knowledge, these results are consistent with the recognized integrative role of OFC in guiding olfactory-based behavior.
evidence: This is an inference about the nature of odor categories.

claim: Orbitofrontal cortex patterns can differentiate between odor objects and categories.
source: Both animal and human studies have demonstrated that OFC patterns can differentiate between odor objects and categories (Howard et al., 2009; Wu et al., 2012; Schoenbaum and Eichenbaum, 1995; Critchley and Rolls, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The orbitofrontal cortex has been proposed to integrate taste and visual information associated with odor stimuli.
source: Moreover, the OFC has been proposed to integrate taste and visual information associated with odor stimuli (Critchley and Rolls, 1996; Gottfried and Dolan, 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The orbitofrontal cortex encodes the reward value of odors.
source: encode the reward value of odors (Howard and Gottfried, 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The orbitofrontal cortex disambiguates mixtures of categorically dissimilar odors.
source: disambiguate mixtures of categorically dissimilar odors (Bowman et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The orbitofrontal cortex represents olfactory lexical-semantic content.
source: and represent olfactory lexical-semantic content (Olofsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The findings highlight the role of orbitofrontal cortex in preserving the perceptual distinctions between different odor categories, likely through its associative access to multimodal and semantic information streams.
source: Viewed in this context, our results highlight the role of OFC in preserving the perceptual distinctions between different odor categories, likely through its associative access to multimodal and semantic information streams.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental findings and prior research.

claim: Single-unit recordings from the hippocampus have identified neurons in both humans and monkeys that are able to categorize visual information.
source: For example, single-unit recordings from the hippocampus have identified neurons in both humans and monkeys that are able to categorize visual information (Kreiman et al., 2000; Hampson et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: fMRI activity in human hippocampus is selectively increased when memory performance relies on perceptual generalization across stimuli.
source: and fMRI activity in human hippocampus is selectively increased when memory performance relies on perceptual generalization across stimuli (Preston et al., 2004; Shohamy and Wagner, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The trend effect of decreased within-category separation in posterior hippocampus in placebo subjects may reflect the role of hippocampus to generalize, or to make inferences, across shared odor features.
source: Considered in this framework, the trend effect of decreased within-category separation in pHIP in placebo subjects may reflect the role of hippocampus to generalize, or to make inferences, across shared odor features, essentially bringing odors of the same category closer together, and creating more separation between different categories (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fMRI pattern data in the context of prior research.

claim: Both piriform cortex and hippocampus have long been regarded as canonical models of autoassociative networks where pattern separation and pattern completion computations can be flexibly achieved.
source: It is interesting to note that both piriform cortex and hippocampus have long been regarded as canonical models of autoassociative networks where pattern separation and pattern completion computations can be flexibly achieved (Yassa and Stark, 2011; Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013; Wilson, 2009; Leutgeb and Leutgeb, 2007; Hunsaker and Kesner, 2013; LaRocque et al., 2013; Eichenbaum et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The effect of baclofen was to impede within-category discrimination in posterior piriform cortex while simultaneously impeding within-category generalization in posterior hippocampus.
source: That the effect of baclofen was to impede within-category discrimination in PPC, while simultaneously impeding within-category generalization in pHIP, highlights a unique functional difference between these two anatomically homologous regions
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings comparing PPC and pHIP.

claim: The findings highlight a unique functional difference between piriform cortex and hippocampus.
source: That the effect of baclofen was to impede within-category discrimination in PPC, while simultaneously impeding within-category generalization in pHIP, highlights a unique functional difference between these two anatomically homologous regions
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental findings.

claim: The findings may help bring new mechanistic understanding of the contributions of piriform cortex, hippocampus, and piriform-hippocampal interactions to human olfactory processing and perception.
source: and may help bring new mechanistic understanding of the contributions of piriform cortex, hippocampus, and piriform-hippocampal interactions to human olfactory processing and perception.
evidence: This is speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: The 50-mg baclofen dose did not impair general cognition or olfactory perceptual performance.
source: Our behavioral data indicate that the 50-mg baclofen dose did not impair general cognition or olfactory perceptual performance
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data.

claim: Off-target effects of the drug were minimal, other than a modest effect on subjective sleepiness that did not interfere with online task accuracy or response times.
source: suggesting that off-target effects of the drug were minimal, other than a modest effect on subjective sleepiness that did not interfere with online task accuracy or response times.
evidence: This is an inference from the behavioral data.

claim: The study medication schedule was similar to those used in other human studies that administered baclofen to induce reliable changes in brain activity or behavior.
source: While it is possible that the 50-mg dose may not have been potent enough to exert a physiological effect, the study medication schedule was similar to those used in other human studies that administered baclofen to induce reliable changes in brain activity or behavior (Terrier et al., 2011; Franklin et al., 2012; Young et al., 2014; Franklin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There was no evidence of drug effect on odor categorization behavior, in spite of significant changes in fMRI pattern representations.
source: In our study, we did not find evidence of drug effect on odor categorization behavior, in spite of significant changes in fMRI pattern representations.
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral and neural findings.

claim: Behavioral tests may not have been sensitive enough to detect changes in perceptual performance.
source: There are at least three possibilities to account for this discrepancy. One possibility is that our behavioral tests were simply not sensitive enough to detect changes in perceptual performance.
evidence: This is speculation about the lack of behavioral effects.

claim: Across both placebo and baclofen groups, there was a general trend towards improved performance, likely reflecting effects of training and exposure.
source: Across both placebo and baclofen groups, there was a general trend towards improved performance, likely reflecting effects of training and exposure.
evidence: This is an inference from the behavioral data.

claim: Changes in piriform odor representations might have induced parallel changes in perception, but other brain areas could compensate for these perturbations, helping to stabilize olfactory perceptual performance.
source: Finally, while changes in piriform odor representations might have induced parallel changes in perception, it is possible that other brain areas would be able to compensate for these perturbations, helping to stabilize olfactory perceptual performance.
evidence: This is speculation about potential compensatory mechanisms.

claim: In the placebo group, increased within-category pattern separation in posterior piriform cortex would be counteracted by decreased within-category pattern separation in posterior hippocampus, resulting in no detectable change at the behavioral level.
source: For example, in the placebo group, increased within-category pattern separation in PPC (Figure 5b) would be counteracted by decreased within-category pattern separation in pHIP (Figure 6b), resulting in no detectable change at the behavioral level.
evidence: This is speculation about how opposing neural changes might cancel out behaviorally.

claim: Baclofen can target GABA(B) receptors in area CA1 of the hippocampus, influencing visual object recognition and memory.
source: One potential issue is that baclofen can also target GABA(B) receptors that have been identified in area CA1 of the hippocampus, influencing visual object recognition and memory (Lanthorn and Cotman, 1981; Ault and Nadler, 1982).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The visual categorization fMRI task confirmed that the pharmacological manipulation induced both regional and modality specificity.
source: This control study confirmed that our pharmacological manipulation induced both regional and modality specificity, thus ruling out possible confounds such as altered global attention, arousal, or hemodynamic reactivity.
evidence: This is an inference from the visual control experiment.

claim: Baclofen was administered systemically.
source: An unavoidable limitation of this study was that baclofen was administered systemically.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: The findings demonstrate regionally selective treatment effects in posterior piriform cortex.
source: While our findings demonstrate regionally selective treatment effects in PPC, it is not possible to confirm that these changes were due to the direct action of baclofen solely at piriform cortex.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings with acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: It is not possible to confirm that the changes in posterior piriform cortex were due to the direct action of baclofen solely at piriform cortex.
source: While our findings demonstrate regionally selective treatment effects in PPC, it is not possible to confirm that these changes were due to the direct action of baclofen solely at piriform cortex.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study.

claim: Baclofen might directly target the layer 1b synapses in piriform cortex where associative intracortical and extracortical inputs predominate.
source: First, baclofen might directly target the layer 1b synapses in piriform cortex where associative intracortical and extracortical inputs predominate.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of baclofen action.

claim: Baclofen might target neurons in orbitofrontal cortex, entorhinal cortex, and other associative brain areas that project onto piriform cortex.
source: Second, baclofen might target neurons in OFC, entorhinal cortex, and other associative brain areas that project onto piriform cortex.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of baclofen action.

claim: The fMRI BOLD response is thought to reflect local dendritic processing and population activity.
source: Given that the fMRI BOLD response is thought to reflect local dendritic processing and population activity (Logothetis and Wandell, 2004; Hipp and Siegel, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The findings in posterior piriform cortex could reflect a distant action of baclofen on orbitofrontal cortex, which in turn alters distributed fMRI patterns measured in piriform cortex.
source: our findings could reflect a distant action of baclofen on OFC (or other areas), which in turn alters distributed fMRI patterns measured in piriform cortex.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of baclofen action.

claim: The changes seen in posterior piriform cortex could theoretically have arisen in the olfactory bulb, where GABA(B) receptors have also been described.
source: Third, the changes seen in PPC could theoretically have arisen in the olfactory bulb, where GABA(B) receptors have also been described (Nickell et al., 1994; Palouzier-Paulignan et al., 2002; Okutani et al., 2003; Wachowiak et al., 2005; Aroniadou-Anderjaska et al., 2000; Isaacson and Vitten, 2003; Karpuk and Hayar, 2008).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to prior research.

claim: If baclofen acted on the olfactory bulb, one might have predicted a more profound olfactory perceptual deficit, including impairments of odor threshold, identification, and perceived intensity.
source: In this instance, one might have predicted a more profound olfactory perceptual deficit, including impairments of odor threshold, identification, and perceived intensity, though such a profile was not found in our study.
evidence: This is speculation about expected outcomes that were not observed.

claim: The findings establish a critical role of the GABA(B) receptor in modulating categorical representations in posterior piriform cortex and orbitofrontal cortex, with specificity for the olfactory modality.
source: Irrespective of the specific mechanism or mechanisms, these findings establish a critical role of the GABA(B) receptor in modulating categorical representations in PPC and OFC, with specificity for the olfactory modality.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: The study provides a foundation for understanding the contribution of afferent and associative inputs to odor categorical perception in the human brain.
source: In summary, our study provides a foundation for understanding the contribution of afferent and associative inputs to odor categorical perception in the human brain.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the study's contribution.

claim: In an earlier study, subjects underwent a 7-day period of odor deprivation, which reduced olfactory afferent input and showed that multivariate pattern representations of odor category were selectively altered in orbitofrontal cortex without any pattern-based changes in posterior piriform cortex.
source: Of note, this work forms a counterpoint to an earlier study from our lab in which subjects underwent a 7-day period of odor deprivation (Wu et al., 2012): by reducing olfactory afferent input, we were able to show that multivariate pattern representations of odor category were selectively altered in OFC, without any pattern-based changes observed in PPC.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In the current study, baclofen was used to reduce olfactory associative input, resulting in a disruption of odor categorization in orbitofrontal cortex and an interference of session-related pattern changes in posterior piriform cortex and posterior hippocampus.
source: By comparison, in the current study, we were able to test the inverse manipulation, using baclofen to reduce olfactory associative input. In this instance, we again observed a disruption of odor categorization in OFC, but also an interference of session-related pattern changes in PPC and pHIP.
evidence: This is a summary of the current study's findings in comparison to prior work.

claim: The fact that within-category pattern changes in posterior piriform cortex were complementary to those in posterior hippocampus, in conjunction with the different course of across-category changes in orbitofrontal cortex, underscores the idea that odor categorization is a dynamic process involving multiple stages of an extended olfactory network.
source: The fact that within-category pattern changes in PPC were complementary to those in pHIP, in conjunction with the different course of across-category changes in OFC, underscores the idea that odor categorization is a dynamic process involving multiple stages of an extended olfactory network.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental findings across multiple brain regions.

claim: Under normal conditions, the ability to refine discriminability of within-category odors in posterior piriform cortex through experience helps to improve perceptual acuity and decision making, and to prevent perceptual generalization from becoming maladaptive.
source: We surmise that under normal conditions, the ability to refine discriminability of within-category odors in PPC through experience helps to improve perceptual acuity and decision making, and to prevent perceptual generalization from becoming maladaptive.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of the findings.

claim: With the interruption of associative input, in the setting of experimental baclofen or even perhaps as the consequence of a neurological disorder, within-category boundaries can become obscured, leading to perceptual over-generalization that can result in detrimental choices.
source: With the interruption of associative input, in the setting of experimental baclofen or even perhaps as the consequence of a neurological disorder, within-category boundaries can become obscured, leading to perceptual over-generalization that can result in detrimental choices.
evidence: This is speculation about the implications of the findings for understanding neurological disorders.

claim: The findings may point toward an important mechanism by which associative networks regulate perceptual processing.
source: As such, our findings may point toward an important mechanism by which associative networks regulate perceptual processing.
evidence: This is speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: Whether such mechanisms are restricted to the olfactory modality, or apply more widely across different sensory systems, remains to be determined.
source: Whether such mechanisms are restricted to the olfactory modality, or apply more widely across different sensory systems, remains to be determined.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of an open question for future research.
